--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.random_k_lift()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Build a random k-lift of the graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.random_k_lift()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Build a random k-lift of the graph. title: >- [Graph.random_k_lift()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Build a random k-lift of the graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Build a random k-lift of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L40197-L40301){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.random_k_lift( k, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Random k-lift](/assets/graphs/random-k-lift.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a triangle on A (accent color), B (teal) and C (violet). Right: a random 3-lift replaces each node with three copies, drawn in its color and labelled A0, A1, A2 and so on, and each edge with a random perfect matching between the copies of its ends, so every copy keeps one neighbor over each original edge. With seed 5 the lift is a single cycle through all nine copies: A0, B1, C1, A1, B2, C0, A2, B0, C2." width="100%"} A k-lift replaces every node `v` with `k` copies `(v, 0), ..., (v, k - 1)` and every edge `u - v` with a perfect matching between the copies of `u` and those of `v`: for a permutation `σ` of `0, ..., k - 1`, copy `(u, i)` is joined to `(v, σ(i))`. A random lift draws each edge's permutation independently and uniformly. Every node of the lift has the degree of the node it copies, and the lift maps onto the original graph as a `k`-fold covering, so local structure is preserved while cycles can unwind into longer ones. Random lifts are the standard way to grow expander graphs (Bilu and Linial, 2006): a lift of a good expander keeps nearly the same spectral gap with high probability while having `k` times as many nodes and the same degrees. They are used to design datacenter networks (Xpander, Valadarsky et al., 2016) and as random models in their own right. A lift can be disconnected, which is more likely when the original graph is a poor expander; it is returned as drawn. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of copies of each node. Must be at least `1` (`k=1` returns a copy). [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. If `None` (default), the permutations differ on each call. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with `k * n` nodes and `k * e` edges, directed if this graph is. Copy `i` of the `j`-th node (in ID order) gets ID `j * k + i + 1`, the label `"(v, i)"` built from the node's label (or its ID if it has none), and the node's attributes. Each edge copy keeps the weight and attributes of the edge it comes from. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `k=` is less than `1`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} One Fisher-Yates shuffle per edge, in edge ID order, so the lift takes $O(k(n + e))$ time. Parallel edges get independent permutations. A self-loop at `v` lifts to the edges `(v, i) - (v, σ(i))`: a self-loop on each fixed point of `σ`, and in an undirected graph a pair of parallel edges for each 2-cycle. Every edge thus has exactly `k` copies, as in NetworkX's `random_k_lift()` on a multigraph (on a simple `nx.Graph`, NetworkX merges those parallel copies). The permutations come from EdgeCase's own generator, so a given seed draws a different lift than NetworkX does. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A 4-lift of the complete graph $K_4$ is a 3-regular graph on 16 nodes: ::: {#0e9a0424 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec k4 = ec.Graph().add_full_graph(4) lift = k4.random_k_lift(4, seed=1) lift.count_nodes(), lift.count_edges(), lift.is_k_regular(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (16, 24, True) ``` ::: ::: Each node of the lift is a copy of a node of the original graph: ::: {#7e98ba7e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} lift.get_node_df().select(["id", "label"]).head(6) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
shape: (6, 2)
idlabel
i64str
1"(1, 0)"
2"(1, 1)"
3"(1, 2)"
4"(1, 3)"
5"(2, 0)"
6"(2, 1)"
``` ::: ::: Lifting a triangle twice either keeps two triangles or unwinds them into a hexagon: ::: {#624871a5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} triangle = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(3) [triangle.random_k_lift(2, seed=s).count_weakly_connected_components() for s in range(6)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1] ``` ::: :::
